text: An expression for a dimensionless quantity P is given by $P=\frac{α}{β}\log _{e}\left (\frac{kt}{βx}\right )$; where $α$ and $β$ are constants, x is distance; k is Boltzmann constant and t is the temperature. Then the dimensions of $α$ will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $P=\frac{α}{β}\log _{e}\left [\frac{kt}{βx}\right ]$

The logarithmic term is dimensionless.

Thus, $[kt/βx]$ is also dimensionless.

i.e. $\frac{[k][t]}{[β][x]}=\left [\mathrm{M}^{0}\mathrm{L}^{0}\mathrm{T}^{0}\right ]$ .......(i)

We have, $E=kt$

Thus, Eq. (i) becomes,

$\begin{array}{l} \frac{\left [\mathrm{M}^{1}\mathrm{L}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\right ]}{[β][\mathrm{L}^{1}]}=\left [\mathrm{M}^{0}\mathrm{L}^{0}\mathrm{T}^{0}\right ] \\  \\ [β]=\left [\mathrm{MLT}^{-2}\right ] \end{array}$

Since, $P$ is also a dimensionless quantity.

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{[α]}{[β]}=\left [\mathrm{M}^{0}\mathrm{L}^{0}\mathrm{T}^{0}\right ] \\  \\ [α]=[β]\left [\mathrm{M}^{0}\mathrm{L}^{0}\mathrm{T}^{0}\right ] \\  \\ [α]=\left [\mathrm{M}^{1}\mathrm{L}^{1}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\right ]=\left [\mathrm{MLT}^{-2}\right ] \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift

text:
If Electric field intensity of a uniform plane electromagnetic wave is given as $E=-301.6\sin (kz-ωt)\widehat{a}_{x}+452.4\sin (kz-ωt)\widehat{a}_{y}\frac{V}{m}$. Then magnetic intensity 'H' of this wave in $Am^{-1}$ will be :

[Given : Speed of light in vacuum $c=3\times 10^{8}$ $ms^{-1}$, Permeability of vacuum $μ_{0}=4π\times 10^{-7}$ $NA^{-2}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The phase $kz-ωt$ shows the wave travels along $+z$, so $⃗{B}=\dfrac{1}{c}\hat{k}\times ⃗{E}$.

Using $\hat{k}\times \hat{a}_{x}=\hat{a}_{y}$ and $\hat{k}\times \hat{a}_{y}=-\hat{a}_{x}$:

$⃗{B}=\dfrac{1}{c}\left [-301.6\sin (kz-ωt)\hat{a}_{y}-452.4\sin (kz-ωt)\hat{a}_{x}\right ]$

The magnetic intensity is $⃗{H}=\dfrac{⃗{B}}{μ_{0}}$, and

$μ_{0}c=4π\times 10^{-7}\times 3\times 10^{8}=120π\approx 377\Omega$

$\dfrac{301.6}{377}=0.8,\dfrac{452.4}{377}=1.2$

$⃗{H}=-0.8\sin (kz-ωt)\hat{a}_{y}-1.2\sin (kz-ωt)\hat{a}_{x}\text{A m}^{-1}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift

text: An electron with speed v and a photon with speed c have the same de-Broglie wavelength. If the kinetic energy and momentum of electron are $E_{e}$ and $p_{e}$ and that of photon are $E_{ph}$ and $p_{ph}$ respectively. Which of the following is correct?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The de Broglie wavelength is $λ=\dfrac{h}{p}$, so equal wavelengths give equal momenta: $p_{e}=p_{ph}=p$.

For the electron, $p=mv$, so $E_{e}=\dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}=\dfrac{pv}{2}$.

For the photon, $E_{ph}=pc$.

$\dfrac{E_{e}}{E_{ph}}=\dfrac{pv/2}{pc}=\dfrac{v}{2c}$

Since $\dfrac{p_{e}}{p_{ph}}=1$, options (C) and (D) are wrong.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift

text:
As per the given circuit, the value of current through the battery will be $____________ A$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The longer plate of the 10 V cell is at the bottom, so the bottom wire (through $2~\Omega$) and the lower-right junction are at the higher potential, while the left wire, joined to the upper plate, is at the lower potential.

$D_{1}$ (top branch) and $D_{3}$ (diagonal branch) point from the higher-potential side towards the left wire, so both are forward biased and conduct like plain wires. $D_{2}$ points from the left wire towards the right side, against the potential difference, so it is reverse biased and its branch carries no current.

With $D_{2}$ removed and $D_{1}$, $D_{3}$ replaced by wires, the circuit becomes:


[IMG]

From the lower-right junction the current reaches the left wire along two paths: up through $10\quad \Omega$ and back through the top $6~\Omega$ ($16\quad \Omega$), or along the diagonal through $6~\Omega$ and $10\quad \Omega$ ($16\quad \Omega$).

$R_{eq}=2+\dfrac{16\times 16}{16+16}=2+8=10\Omega$

$I=\dfrac{V}{R_{eq}}=\dfrac{10}{10}=1\text{A}$

Hence, the answer is 1.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift

text:
A 110 V, 50 Hz, AC source is connected in the circuit (as shown in figure). The current through the resistance 55 $\Omega$, at resonance in the circuit, will be $__________ A$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the circuit, the inductor $L$ and the capacitor $C$ are in parallel with each other, and this $LC$ combination is in series with the $55\Omega$ resistor and the source.

In the ideal parallel $LC$ combination the branch currents $\dfrac{V}{X_{L}}$ and $\dfrac{V}{X_{C}}$ are opposite in phase, so

$\frac{1}{Z_{LC}}=\left |\frac{1}{X_{L}}-\frac{1}{X_{C}}\right |$

At resonance $X_{L}=X_{C}$, so $\dfrac{1}{Z_{LC}}=0$, i.e. $Z_{LC}\to \infty$.

The impedance of the whole circuit therefore tends to infinity, and the current drawn from the source, which is the current through the $55\Omega$ resistor, is

$I=\frac{110}{Z}=0$

The value $\dfrac{110}{55}=2\text{A}$ would apply only to a series $LCR$ circuit at resonance, which is not the arrangement here.

Hence, the answer is 0.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th June Morning Shift
